title: All confidential OIDC clients share the literal client secret "secret", including the public MAUI client
owner_hint: top committer: Michael Stonis (1 of 1 recent commit); no CODEOWNERS entry
rationale: All three clients register the same literal secret and the MAUI binary ships it, with webapp also disabling PKCE. The diff loads per-client secrets from ClientSecrets:{clientId} with fail-closed lookup, makes MAUI a public client (no secret, PKCE retained), enables PKCE for webapp, and reads the relying-party secrets from configuration.
variants_checked: Server and both relying parties plus the MAUI default changed; swagger clients are intentionally public; no other committed client-secret literals found.
bypass_considered: MAUI remains a public client whose client_id and custom scheme are known; PKCE stops code interception but not a malicious app starting its own flow. Distinct secrets rely on operational config.
test_note: Added ConfidentialClientsUseConfiguredSecretsAndPkce and extended the existing config dictionary.
review_reason: Secret removal is root-cause, but the patch adds required ClientSecrets/ClientSecret keys without supplying them in appsettings or AppHost, so Identity.API and both relying parties throw at startup; the unit fixture hides it with dummy values. It also mixes in webapp PKCE changes that belong to a separate finding.
